bull.b: Very low leverage reduces fixed financial obligations and preserves flexibility while the company advances clinical programs. A lightly indebted balance sheet may make it easier to allocate future capital toward research and development rather than interest payments, although losses remain material.

The improvement in annual losses and cash burn indicates some expense discipline within the early-stage operating model. If sustained, better cost control could extend available resources and reduce the pace of external funding needed while clinical development continues.

A concentrated pipeline around CCL24 and fibro-inflammatory diseases gives Chemomab a clear development focus rather than a broad, unfocused portfolio. This specialization can support efficient research prioritization and consistent scientific positioning as programs advance.

bear.b: Continued absence of revenue means Chemomab has not yet demonstrated commercial traction or an operating model capable of funding itself. The company therefore remains dependent on successful clinical progress and eventual commercialization to establish sustainable earnings.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow limits financial independence and makes future development reliant on additional capital. Even with improved 2025 burn, financing needs can constrain program choices and increase vulnerability if funding conditions become less favorable.

The proposed redomiciliation and Scipher merger could materially reshape Chemomab, but completion depends on regulatory approvals, shareholder action, financing, and other execution steps. Delays or failure would disrupt the planned strategic path and add uncertainty to development funding.
